patch.description: A partial settings document. Secrets are write-only (`secret_key`, `password`, `client_secret`); an empty string removes one. Read-only fields may be sent back and are ignored. Keys in `managed` answer 409 and invalid values 422; in both cases nothing is saved. Changing `auth.mode` signs out every other session, and switching to `header` from a connection that isn't from a trusted proxy is refused with 409.

post.description: Probes the public URL the way Alexa would: an unsigned POST to `/api/v1/alexa` must be answered 400 by Encore; the TLS certificate must be trusted and the endpoint must accept TLS 1.2, the only version Alexa offers; and, for information, whether other `/api/v1` routes are reachable through the proxy too (they always need a sign-in). Redirects are not followed. Needs an admin session or, before the admin account exists, the setup token (403 if it's wrong). A certificate that expires within 14 days is only a warning.

get.description: return_urls must be listed under the security profile's Allowed Return URLs. Over HTTPS the consent page returns to Encore's callback; otherwise to the local address, whose URL the user pastes back. Until the client ID and secret are saved, url is empty and only return_urls is filled in, so they can be shown while the security profile is being created. A pending authorisation's state and PKCE verifier stay on the server for 15 minutes.
